content:
MARTA KOWAL-BRANDT
Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps | QA Automation Engineer
Wroclaw, Poland | marta.kowalbrandt@example.com | +48 555 303 303 | gitlab.com/mkb-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
QA automation engineer with 7 years of experience, including 2+ years focused on CI/CD, test infrastructure and build tooling. Owns GitLab CI pipelines and builds short-lived test environments using Docker and Helm on a shared Kubernetes cluster. Personal infrastructure projects include a k3s homelab with GitOps-based deployments and Terraform-provisioned Hetzner VPS infrastructure. Brings a measured, analytical approach to improving reliability and delivery, and experience documenting technical processes and mentoring interns. Moving toward a full-time DevOps / platform engineering role.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Infrastructure and delivery: GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Docker Compose, Helm, Kubernetes (namespace-level access; test environments), Terraform (personal projects), Argo CD
Monitoring and data: Grafana, Prometheus, Loki, PostgreSQL
Programming and automation: Python, Bash, Java (test code), SQL, Ansible (basic)
Testing: pytest, Playwright, Selenium, Postman
Systems: Linux, Git, k3s, Traefik, cert-manager
Cloud learning: AWS EC2 and S3 basics (personal learning)

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure) | Odrava Health Software | Wroclaw | 2021–Present
- Own GitLab CI pipelines for 3 product teams (approximately 25 developers), covering build, unit, integration and end-to-end test stages and artifact publishing.
- Reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes by parallelising test jobs, caching dependencies and separating end-to-end tests into their own stage; monthly CI runner costs decreased by about 30%.
- Built merge-request ephemeral test environments with Docker Compose and later Helm charts deployed to the company's shared Kubernetes cluster. Each environment includes the application, PostgreSQL and seeded data; environments are automatically removed after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.
- Maintain a pytest and Playwright end-to-end suite of approximately 900 tests; reduced the flaky test rate from 7% to below 1%.
- Built a flaky-test dashboard by collecting CI results in PostgreSQL and visualising trends in Grafana, helping teams identify and address recurring failures.
- Wrote Bash and Python tooling for PostgreSQL test-data seeding and authored an internal guide to CI used in onboarding.
- Mentored 2 QA interns in 2023.

QA Engineer | Brightmill Software House | Wroclaw | 2019–2021
- Tested web and mobile applications for client projects through manual and automated testing.
- Introduced a Java and Selenium automated regression suite for the largest client project, replacing a full regression process that had previously taken two people three days.
- Configured Jenkins jobs to run nightly regression tests.

Customer Support Specialist (2nd line) | Brightmill Software House | 2018–2019
- Investigated customer issues using logs and databases, and reproduced bugs for developers.

SELECTED INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECTS
Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps | Personal | 2024–2025
- Built a three-node Raspberry Pi 5 k3s cluster and deployed applications from a Git repository using Argo CD.
- Set up Prometheus, Grafana and Loki for monitoring, Traefik ingress and cert-manager for TLS.
- Provisioned infrastructure for a small Hetzner VPS with Terraform; used Ansible at a basic level.

Merge-Request Ephemeral Environments | Odrava Health | 2023–2024
- Implemented short-lived environments for merge requests, deployed through GitLab CI and Helm to the shared Kubernetes cluster.
- Enabled QA and product reviewers to assess features before merge, with end-to-end tests running against each environment.
- Automated environment cleanup after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.

CI Pipeline Speed-up | Odrava Health | 2022
- Profiled pipelines across three teams, parallelised test jobs, added dependency caching and separated end-to-end tests into a dedicated stage.
- Reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes and monthly CI runner costs by about 30%.

EDUCATION
BEng Computer Engineering | Silesian Lowlands University of Technology | 2018

CERTIFICATIONS AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
ISTQB Foundation Level | 2019
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) exam booked for January 2027; currently studying
Terraform Associate practice tests completed; certification exam not taken

LANGUAGES
Polish (native) | English (C1) | German (A2)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with clear progression from QA automation toward DevOps and platform engineering. It uses quantified achievements effectively, including reducing pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes, lowering runner costs by approximately 30%, and reducing flaky tests from 7% to below 1%. The Professional Summary is credible and appropriately transparent about the candidate’s current scope, including namespace-level Kubernetes access, personal Terraform work, and the transition toward DevOps. The selected infrastructure projects add useful evidence and make the career direction easy to understand. The main content limitation is that several achievements relevant to leadership, communication, documentation, stakeholder enablement, and observability are present but could be connected more explicitly to the target role’s terminology.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-compatible: it uses standard section headings, plain text formatting, conventional job titles, recognizable technology names, chronological experience, and measurable results. Relevant keywords such as infrastructure, CI/CD, Terraform, Kubernetes, Helm, GitOps, Linux, monitoring, TLS, PostgreSQL, AWS, and system-relevant tooling are present. AI screening probability is good because the document clearly explains the context and scope of the technologies rather than merely listing them. Alignment would improve slightly if the document explicitly used supported terms such as technical documentation, stakeholder collaboration, observability, certificate management, and infrastructure operation. It should not add Terragrunt, mTLS, production cloud ownership, or stronger Terraform claims because those are not supported by the candidate information.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document presents a credible adjacent match rather than a direct match for this contractor role. It shows hands-on infrastructure-related work through GitLab CI ownership, ephemeral environments, Docker, Helm, namespace-level Kubernetes work, monitoring, and personal k3s and Hetzner infrastructure. It also demonstrates analytical thinking and communication through quantified pipeline optimisation, the flaky-test dashboard, internal CI documentation, and mentoring. AWS basics, Linux, virtual-machine-based Hetzner infrastructure, and JVM-related Java test code are represented. However, the candidate material indicates gaps in strong Terraform and Terragrunt, mTLS, production cloud infrastructure operation, IoT or remote-device integration, and direct backend/full-stack experience. The CV correctly avoids claiming these capabilities. The candidate also has limited evidence of leading cross-functional technical proposals or operating production infrastructure, so the fit is stronger for a junior-to-mid DevOps/platform position than for a fully independent infrastructure contractor shaping train-to-cloud architecture from the start. Company-culture alignment is only lightly expressed; ownership, collaboration, and enabling other teams are evidenced, but the CV does not need extensive culture language.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, HIGH-VALUE ENHANCEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, revise the final two sentences to connect existing evidence more directly to the role’s terminology without overstating seniority. For example: “Brings a measured, analytical approach to improving reliability and delivery, with experience documenting technical processes, mentoring interns, and enabling QA and product stakeholders to review changes safely. Moving toward a full-time DevOps / platform engineering role focused on infrastructure automation, observability, and reliable delivery.”
2. In the Odrava Health Software experience, revise the bullet about the internal guide to make the communication and enablement impact explicit: “Wrote and maintained an internal guide to CI used in onboarding, helping developers and QA engineers understand pipeline stages, test execution, and artifact publishing.” This is supported by the candidate’s notes and better matches the requirement for clear communication and bringing stakeholders along.
3. In the Odrava Health Software experience, revise the ephemeral-environment bullet to include the existing stakeholder outcome: “Built merge-request ephemeral test environments with Docker Compose and later Helm charts deployed with GitLab CI to the company’s shared Kubernetes cluster; enabled QA and product reviewers to assess features before merge, with automatic cleanup after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.”
4. In the Selected Infrastructure Projects section under “Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps,” change “Set up Prometheus, Grafana and Loki for monitoring, Traefik ingress and cert-manager for TLS” to “Set up Prometheus, Grafana and Loki for observability, Traefik ingress, and cert-manager for TLS certificate management.” This uses terminology from the advertisement while remaining fully supported.
5. In the Technical Skills section, change “Terraform (personal projects)” to “Terraform (personal Hetzner VPS infrastructure)” and retain the existing “AWS EC2 and S3 basics (personal learning)” wording. This keeps the scope precise and prevents an ATS or recruiter from interpreting the CV as claiming substantial commercial cloud or Terraform ownership.
6. In the Technical Skills section, consider changing “Kubernetes (namespace-level access; test environments)” to “Kubernetes (namespace-level access; Helm-deployed test environments)” so the candidate’s practical scope and deployment experience are immediately clear.
7. In the Certifications and Professional Development section, retain the current wording for the CKA and Terraform Associate items. Do not label either as a certification or imply that either exam has been passed; the current wording is appropriately truthful.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, credible CV for a QA-to-DevOps transition. It is well structured, metric-driven and professional, with especially effective evidence around GitLab CI ownership, pipeline optimisation, ephemeral environments, Kubernetes usage, observability and test reliability. The quantified results—pipeline time reduced from 38 to 14 minutes, runner costs reduced by approximately 30%, and flaky tests reduced from 7% to below 1%—give the document strong impact. The Professional Summary accurately explains the transition without overstating production infrastructure ownership. The main content limitation is that the Selected Infrastructure Projects section repeats several achievements already described under Odrava Health, using valuable space that could instead clarify infrastructure scope, architecture decisions, networking or stakeholder leadership.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-compatible: it uses conventional headings, readable text, standard employment chronology, clear skill categories and relevant terms such as GitLab CI, Kubernetes, Helm, Docker, Terraform, AWS, Linux, Prometheus, Grafana, TLS and Argo CD. No tables, graphics, icons or complex formatting appear likely to interfere with parsing. Keyword coverage is strong for CI/CD, test infrastructure and Kubernetes-oriented DevOps roles. AI screening probability is good for junior-to-mid DevOps, platform engineering and test-infrastructure roles, but only moderate for this specific contractor role because the CV does not demonstrate or contain strong evidence for Terragrunt, mTLS, systems architecture, cloud production operation, security engineering or stakeholder-led technical proposals. The AWS wording is appropriately qualified as learning rather than professional experience.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns well with the hands-on infrastructure aspect of the role through GitLab CI ownership, Docker and Helm deployments, namespace-level Kubernetes work, ephemeral environments, Terraform-based personal infrastructure, monitoring and Linux. It also demonstrates ownership, analytical thinking and clear technical communication through pipeline profiling, measurable optimisation, internal documentation and mentoring. The use of Argo CD, Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Traefik and cert-manager supports the platform-observability aspects of the role. However, the candidate's own material indicates gaps in several core requirements: no Terragrunt, no mTLS experience, no professional AWS/cloud infrastructure operation, no stated production on-call ownership, and no IoT, automotive or remote-device integration. The material also does not establish strong systems-architecture or practical security-engineering experience. The candidate has Java test-code experience, but not the backend/JVM background described as a nice-to-have. These are job-fit gaps rather than defects in the CV and should not be implied as qualifications.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, replace “Moving toward a full-time DevOps / platform engineering role” with a more role-relevant but equally truthful closing sentence such as: “Targeting a DevOps or platform engineering role focused on CI/CD, containerised environments, infrastructure automation and observability.” This uses the job’s terminology without claiming production cloud or architecture experience.
2. In Technical Skills, change “Terraform (personal projects)” to “Terraform (personal infrastructure projects)” and change “Cloud learning: AWS EC2 and S3 basics (personal learning)” to “AWS: EC2 and S3 basics (personal learning only).” This keeps the scope explicit while improving keyword matching and preventing recruiters from interpreting the experience as professional AWS operation.
3. In the Odrava Health experience section, revise “Built merge-request ephemeral test environments...” to explicitly include the supported stakeholder outcome: “Built and operated merge-request ephemeral test environments with Docker Compose and later Helm on the company’s shared Kubernetes cluster, enabling QA and product reviewers to validate changes before merge.” This better matches the role’s emphasis on operating environments and bringing stakeholders along.
4. In the Odrava Health experience section, revise the internal-guide bullet to: “Authored the internal ‘How our CI Works’ guide used in onboarding, documenting pipeline stages, test environments and CI operating practices.” This makes the communication and technical-documentation evidence more searchable and specific without adding unsupported responsibilities.
5. Reduce duplication between Professional Experience and Selected Infrastructure Projects. Keep the Homelab k3s Cluster and Flaky Test Dashboard projects, but either remove the duplicated “Merge-Request Ephemeral Environments” and “CI Pipeline Speed-up” project entries or replace them with a compact “Selected Technical Achievements” subsection containing one-line results. The current repetition is not an ATS defect, but it makes the CV longer without adding much new evidence.
6. In the Systems section of Technical Skills, change “cert-manager for TLS” to “Traefik ingress; cert-manager for SSL/TLS certificate management.” This is supported by the candidate’s project information and improves matching for the job’s SSL/TLS terminology. Do not add mTLS, network design or security engineering claims, because those are not supported by the candidate information.
7. In the Certifications and Professional Development section, retain the current wording that the CKA exam is booked and the Terraform exam was not taken. Do not shorten these entries to “CKA” or “Terraform Associate,” since the current wording correctly prevents them from being misread as completed certifications.

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is well structured, readable, professional, and unusually strong on quantified QA infrastructure outcomes. The summary establishes the transition toward DevOps, while the experience and project sections provide credible evidence through GitLab CI ownership, ephemeral environments, Kubernetes, Terraform personal projects, monitoring, and measurable pipeline improvements. The main content limitation is that some of the strongest transferable evidence—technical documentation, mentoring, stakeholder enablement, and analytical investigation—is not consistently framed in the job's language. The selected projects also partly duplicate the Odrava experience, although the duplication is relevant and not excessive.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document uses standard ATS-friendly headings, simple text formatting, conventional dates, and searchable technology names such as Terraform, Kubernetes, Helm, GitLab CI, Docker, AWS, Linux, Grafana, Prometheus, and TLS. It should parse reliably. ATS alignment is reduced because the CV cannot truthfully demonstrate several central terms from the advertisement: Terragrunt, systems architecture/system design, networking beyond ingress/TLS, mTLS, practical security, and virtual machines. The explicit scope clarification around namespace-level Kubernetes access and personal AWS learning improves credibility, but the headline and summary may still cause some automated systems to interpret the candidate as a more experienced cloud infrastructure engineer than the evidence supports. Overall AI screening probability is moderate: strong keyword and evidence coverage for CI/CD, containers, Kubernetes test environments, observability, and analytical improvement, but limited coverage of the advertisement's core cloud architecture and security requirements.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns well with hands-on delivery automation, infrastructure-adjacent engineering, Linux, Kubernetes-based test environments, observability, analytical improvement, documentation, and working with QA/product stakeholders. It also shows AWS exposure at a basic personal-learning level and JVM exposure through Java test automation. The candidate's evidence is weaker than the role's requirements for strong Terraform and Terragrunt, end-to-end cloud environment design and operation, systems architecture, mTLS, network design, practical security, production operation, and IoT/remote-device integration. The CV does not show a backend or full-stack background; Java is limited to test code. These are candidate-experience gaps rather than defects that can be solved through rewriting. The ownership, analytical, collaborative, and technical-enablement aspects of the company culture are reasonably supported by pipeline ownership, documentation, mentoring, and enabling QA/product review.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL ISSUES: None identified; the document is consistent with the Original Candidate Information and does not contain apparent hallucinated skills, tools, certifications, or experience.

MINOR, HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, replace the final sentence, "Moving toward a full-time DevOps / platform engineering role," with a more job-relevant but still accurate statement such as: "Targets infrastructure engineering and DevOps roles focused on CI/CD, containerised test environments, infrastructure automation, observability, and reliable delivery." This removes the less useful emphasis on the career transition while preserving truthful scope.
2. In the Odrava Health Software experience section, revise the first bullet to use the advertisement's operational language without overstating production ownership: "Own and operate GitLab CI pipelines for 3 product teams (approximately 25 developers), covering build, unit, integration and end-to-end test stages and artifact publishing." Keep the existing quantified result in the next bullet.
3. In the Odrava experience section, add a separate bullet after the ephemeral-environment bullet: "Documented the CI platform and authored an internal guide used in onboarding; mentored 2 QA interns in 2023." This brings the candidate's documented communication, enablement, and leadership evidence into the main experience section rather than leaving it mainly in the summary.
4. In the Merge-Request Ephemeral Environments project, revise the stakeholder outcome bullet to make the collaboration evidence more explicit: "Enabled QA and product reviewers to assess features before merge, with end-to-end tests running against each environment." This is already supported by the original portfolio and directly supports bringing stakeholders along.
5. In the Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps project, clarify the infrastructure scope in the Terraform bullet: "Provisioned a small Hetzner VPS with Terraform and used Ansible at a basic level; deployed and operated monitoring, ingress, and TLS components on a personal three-node k3s cluster." This makes the infrastructure operation evidence clearer without implying ownership of a production cloud platform or Kubernetes cluster administration at work.
6. In the Technical Skills section, change the heading "Cloud learning" to "Cloud exposure" and retain the qualification: "AWS EC2 and S3 basics (personal learning); Hetzner VPS infrastructure provisioned with Terraform (personal project)." This is more searchable and precise while clearly distinguishing learning and personal-project experience from professional cloud operation.
7. In the Technical Skills section, change "Systems: Linux, Git, k3s, Traefik, cert-manager" to "Systems and networking: Linux, Git, k3s, Traefik ingress, cert-manager, TLS." Only use "TLS," not "mTLS" or "SSL/TLS," because the original information supports TLS but does not establish mutual TLS or SSL/TLS implementation experience.
8. In the Certifications and Professional Development section, keep the current non-completion wording, but format it consistently as: "Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) — exam scheduled January 2027; not yet certified" and "HashiCorp Terraform Associate — practice tests completed; exam not taken." This reduces any risk that a recruiter or ATS interprets either item as an obtained certification.
